from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
reader=PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('Pages:', len(reader.pages))
print('Metadata:', reader.metadata)
parts=[]
for i,p in enumerate(reader.pages,1):
    t=p.extract_text()
    parts.append(f'\\n\\n--- PAGE {i} ---\\n\\n'+t)
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text(''.join(parts))
print('Total characters:',sum(map(len,parts)))
print(''.join(parts[:3]))
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses a relevant NLP problem: improving instruction tuning using existing supervision. Its three-stage recipe is understandable and adapts Mixup to autoregressive response-token representations without requiring additional response annotations.

The empirical coverage is substantial. Table 1 reports improvements across seven model–dataset settings spanning three model families and three training corpora, with approximately 0.20–0.40-point gains on MT-Bench and consistently higher length-controlled AlpacaEval-2 win rates.

Additional evaluations support the direction of the results. Medical QA accuracy improves by 1.33 and 1.66 percentage points on average for Llama and Mistral. The human study reports 42.5% preference for SFTMix versus 26.5% for NTP, with 31% ties, across 200 judgments on 80 prompts.

The experiments investigate several useful implementation choices, including retaining the NTP objective, regularization strength, confidence partition sizes, weaker reference models, data selection, and LoRA. The manuscript is generally well organized and provides the principal optimization hyperparameters.
weaknesses: The central claim that confidence-based pairing is crucial is insufficiently isolated. There is no ordinary random-pair Mixup baseline, within-confidence pairing comparison, or comparison against confidence from a single checkpoint. Section 5.2 changes the dataset by introducing GPT-4 responses but does not evaluate confidence-based pairing on that same modified dataset. Consequently, its negative quality-based result cannot establish the proposed pairing strategy's advantage. The methodological distinction from the cited cartography-based Mixup work of Park and Caragea (2022) also needs clearer treatment.

The evaluation protocol leaves uncertainty about the reported gains. Appendix A.1 selects both hyperparameters using MT-Bench and AlpacaEval-2, which are also the final evaluation benchmarks; no separate validation protocol is described. Five evaluation rounds do not establish robustness across independently trained models, and confidence intervals or paired significance analyses are absent. The consistency across configurations is encouraging, but benchmark-based selection and unquantified training variability prevent a clear positive Findings recommendation.

The proposed mechanism is stronger than the supporting evidence. A t-SNE plot of confidence extremes and a 7% reduction in training-confidence standard deviation do not demonstrate reduced overfitting on confident examples or improved generalization on unconfident examples. Section 3.4 establishes that the auxiliary objective changes gradients, without establishing either benefit. Because interpolation occurs immediately before a linear head, it is also equivalent to interpolating logits. Held-out analyses by confidence group and controls for topic, response length, and label noise would better substantiate the semantic interpretation.

Reproducibility remains incomplete despite the supplied optimizer settings. Missing details include reference-checkpoint timing, sequence-length limits and chat formatting, exact judge versions and generation settings, and LoRA configuration. No implementation or configuration release is linked. The human study also omits annotator counts, judgment allocation across prompts, and blinding or agreement information, limiting assessment of this corroborating evidence.

The practical cost is insufficiently characterized. SFTMix requires reference-model fine-tuning and checkpoint-based scoring in addition to target-model training, but total GPU time, memory overhead, and performance under matched compute budgets are not reported. The weaker-reference and LoRA experiments are useful initial evidence, but do not establish the overall cost-effectiveness suggested by the discussion of compute-constrained use.

Several technical explanations need correction. The losses use negative cross-entropy while Section 3.4 differentiates positive cross-entropy, creating a sign inconsistency. Section 5.3's distinction between an additional loss and a regularizer is operationally a change in its coefficient. Appendix A.1 incorrectly describes Beta(0.1, 0.1) as flat and producing examples far from the endpoints; it concentrates near the endpoints. These are correctable exposition issues rather than evidence that the implementation necessarily used an incorrect objective.
